How to Use the Smart BOQ Estimator & Construction Calculator

Our automated civil engineering suite provides instant material calculations based on current Pakistani market rates. To compute an accurate Bill of Quantities (BOQ), select your target project location (e.g., Lahore, Karachi, Islamabad), input standard plot sizes such as 5 Marla, 10 Marla, or 1 Kanal, and specify structural dimensions including covered area and floor heights.

Understanding Material Cost Distribution

The integrated mathematical modules parse raw dimension boundaries to formulate localized breakdowns for vital infrastructure components. This includes exact calculations for brick counts, concrete volumetric ratios (sand, cement, crush/gravel distributions), reinforcing steel reinforcement weights in tons, and associated manual labor wages required for structural grey structures.

Complete Guide to Construction Cost Estimation in Pakistan

Planning a construction project requires precise calculations and up-to-date market rates. Intextify Construction Suite is designed to help homeowners, contractors, and civil engineers generate accurate Bill of Quantities (BOQ) and cost estimates instantly.

Understanding the BOQ Estimator

A reliable BOQ ensures that your project stays within budget. Our tool uses live market rates for essential materials like Bricks, Cement, Sand, Crush, and Labor. It automatically calculates the required quantities based on your plot size and covered area. Proper estimation of foundational Earthfill is also critical for structural integrity before masonry begins.

How the Steel Calculator Works

Our integrated Steel Calculator uses the D²/162 formula for metric (meters) and D²/533 for Imperial (feet), ensuring 100% accuracy in structural cost estimates.

Why Use Live Material Rates?

Construction material costs fluctuate daily. By leveraging automated daily rate scraping, Intextify ensures your estimates reflect true current market conditions in Pakistan.

What is PCC (Plain Cement Concrete)?

PCC stands for Plain Cement Concrete — a mixture of cement, sand, and aggregate without steel reinforcement. Primarily used for firm, level bases for footings and floors.

What is RCC (Reinforced Cement Concrete)?

RCC includes steel bars embedded in concrete, providing high tensile strength for structural elements like beams, columns, and slabs.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

How does this calculator account for dry volume?

Dry materials take up 54% more volume than wet concrete. Multiply wet volume × 1.54 to get required dry material volume before purchase.

What is the difference between M15 and M20 concrete?

M15 (1:2:4) is for regular slabs and non-load-bearing elements. M20 (1:1.5:3) has higher cement content and is required for load-bearing columns and heavy structural beams.

How many cement bags for a 10×10 ft slab?

A 10×10 ft slab at 6 inches thick (50 cft wet volume) requires approximately 11 bags of cement using M15 mix. Use the calculator above for your exact dimensions.

Why is the dry volume factor 1.54?

When water is added, fine aggregates fill voids between coarse aggregates, shrinking the overall volume by ~35%. The 1.54 factor compensates to ensure correct dry material quantities are purchased.

Steel Reinforcement Cost & Weight Estimation

Accurate estimation of steel (rebar) is critical for structural stability and cost control. Our integrated Steel Calculator automatically computes weight using standard engineering formulas.

Metric Formula (kg/m)

When measuring steel bar lengths in meters, the weight per meter is calculated as: Weight = D² / 162 (Where D is the diameter in mm).

Imperial Formula (kg/ft)

In Pakistan, lengths are often measured in feet. The weight per foot is calculated as: Weight = D² / 533 (Where D is the diameter in mm).

Civil Engineering Glossary

Bill of Quantities (BOQ)
A detailed document used in tendering in the construction industry in which materials, parts, and labor (and their costs) are itemized.
Plain Cement Concrete (PCC)
A mixture of cement, sand, and aggregate without any steel reinforcement, typically used as a foundational leveling course.
Reinforced Cement Concrete (RCC)
Concrete that contains embedded steel bars (rebar) to provide high tensile strength, used in slabs, beams, and columns.
Marla to Square Feet Conversion in Pakistan
A Marla is a traditional unit of land area. In Lahore, 1 Marla is generally equal to 225 square feet, while in other regions it may be 272 square feet.
Steel Grade 60 vs Grade 40
Grade 60 steel has a minimum yield strength of 60,000 psi and is standard for commercial and major residential load-bearing structures. Grade 40 (40,000 psi) is typically used for minor, non-load-bearing elements.
